speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To better understand your current symptoms, can you describe the exact location and nature of the shooting pain you are experiencing in your ear? Additionally, how long has it been since your tympanoplasty surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain occurring specifically when you eat suggests involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve; is the sensation in your ear accompanied by temporary dryness of your mouth or tongue? Also, have you noticed any recent changes in the sensation of your right ear, such as tingling or a "full" feeling?

REQUEST TEST: Tympanometry and audiogram review.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tympanometry and audiogram review indicate improved hearing by 20 decibels post tympanoplasty as per the audiology report from one week ago. No specific tympanometry results were provided in the data to confirm middle ear pressure or compliance status.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (also known as Frey's Syndrome or post-surgical nerve irritation). The combination of shooting pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and discomfort with earrings, following a tympanoplasty, strongly points to irritation or neuropathic pain in the auriculotemporal nerve rather than a middle ear fluid issue, especially given the normal tympanometry.
